facts.claim: The Counted Lots gathers or works a resource the player can see.
A unique item is kept at The Counted Lots.
A quest starts or turns at The Counted Lots.
Materials are gathered or stacked at The Counted Lots.
Diver families work a pearl bed that is divided into numbered lots.
The bed lies in clear water over a firm bed inside an offshore bar, six to nine metres down.
The diver families hold the numbered lots by inheritance.
The families share the tenders moored over the lots.
The deep lots pay best and they kill divers.
A diver's tally records the lots worked, with the deep lots entered in a second hand.
Marker buoys and a tender boat float over water with no bed in sight.
Keg buoys, grading baskets and stone lot cairns mark the lots.
A tally book records the drownings as well as the takings.
A lot with no living heir has to be reassigned. The claimant pays a fraction of the lot's value to the heirs' line.
A unique item lies among the lots.
Workshop stock of materials can be found.
The lots are found by spotting the tender boat.
The lots are worked daily.
The mood is businesslike about a dangerous trade.
The keg buoys are grey-brown.
The water is green and the shell silver.
Rope creaks above.
Shell clicks into a basket below.
If foreigners learned to dive here, the lot system collapses.
The diver families teach their own.
